step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 32-year-old pregnant woman whose fetus was affected by congenital Zika syndrome via sexual transmission from partner

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnosis of congenital Zika virus syndrome transmitted sexually during pregnancy

evidence_items.source_quote: confirmation was received from the CDC that all placental samples were positive for Zika RNA, thus supporting the diagnosis of congenital Zika syndrome.

rationale: A 32-year-old woman whose infant had microcephaly (<1st percentile) following paternal travel to Haiti and sexual transmission during pregnancy. CDC evaluation confirmed that all placental samples were positive for Zika RNA by RT-PCR (E1 confirmatory evidence), establishing congenital Zika syndrome. Single patient dyad, current active gestational episode, primary diagnosis confirmed. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 46-year-old female presenting with acute fever, rash, and brachial vein thrombosis

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnosis of acute Zika virus infection complicated by upper extremity deep venous thrombosis

evidence_items.source_quote: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test confirmed Zika infection.

rationale: A 46-year-old female presenting with high fever, arthralgia, cutaneous rash, and acute right brachial vein thrombosis. Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing confirmed acute Zika infection (E1 confirmatory evidence). Single patient, current episode, primary diagnosis confirmed. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 53-year-old male presenting with acute febrile arthralgia and popliteal vein thrombosis

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnosis of acute Zika virus infection complicated by popliteal vein thrombosis

evidence_items.source_quote: He also tested positive for Zika virus.

rationale: A 53-year-old male presenting with acute fever, asthenia, arthralgia, and left popliteal vein deep vein thrombosis. PCR testing confirmed positive for Zika virus (E1 confirmatory evidence). Single patient, current active episode, primary diagnosis confirmed. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 45-year-old male traveler returning from Brazil with acute Zika infection and prolonged seminal shedding

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnosis of acute Zika virus infection with persistent viral RNA excretion in semen

evidence_items.source_quote: On day 3 of his illness, Zika virus RNA was detected in urine but not in serum; Zika virus IgM and IgG were not detected in serum by an ELISA IgM and IgG kit (EUROIMMUN AG, Lubeck, Germany).

rationale: A 45-year-old male traveler returning from Rio de Janeiro, Brazil with acute fever, retro-orbital headache, arthralgia, and maculopapular rash. Zika virus RNA was detected by RT-PCR in urine on day 3 and serially in semen up to 92 days, with subsequent serum IgM/IgG seroconversion (E1 confirmatory evidence). Single patient, current episode, primary diagnosis confirmed. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Stillborn male neonate with congenital Zika syndrome, microcephaly, and arthrogryposis

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnosis of Congenital Zika syndrome confirmed by postmortem CSF RT-PCR

evidence_items.source_quote: The RT-PCR for ZIKV/Dengue/Chikungunya in the patient's cerebrospinal fluid detected the presence of Zika viral RNA.

rationale: A stillborn male neonate delivered at 35 weeks gestation presenting with severe congenital anomalies including microcephaly, arthrogryposis, right radial aplasia, and lissencephaly following maternal first-trimester rash illness during the 2016 Zika outbreak in Mexico. RT-PCR performed on the patient's cerebrospinal fluid detected Zika viral RNA (E1 confirmatory evidence). Single patient, current episode, primary diagnosis confirmed. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Male in his 40s with Guillain-Barré syndrome and confirmed Zika virus infection

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnosis of acute Zika virus infection triggering Guillain-Barré syndrome

evidence_items.source_quote: A urine sample, taken at day two after admission, was tested positive for ZIKV RNA with a Ct-value of 35.7.

rationale: A male in his 40s presenting with Guillain-Barré syndrome following a flu-like illness. A urine sample collected 2 days after admission tested positive for ZIKV RNA by real-time RT-PCR with a Ct value of 35.7 (E1 confirmatory evidence). Single patient, current episode, primary diagnosis confirmed. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 38-year-old postpartum breastfeeding mother with acute Zika virus infection

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnosis of acute Zika virus infection in postpartum mother confirmed by RT-PCR

evidence_items.source_quote: ZIKV RNA was still detected in the mother's urine until December 26 but not in blood.

rationale: A 38-year-old postpartum woman presenting with acute low-grade fever, itchy maculopapular rash, bilateral conjunctivitis, and polyarthralgia. Real-time RT-PCR detected ZIKV RNA in consecutive breast milk samples and serial urine specimens (E1 confirmatory evidence). Single patient, current episode, primary diagnosis confirmed. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 29-year-old pregnant traveler with acute Zika infection and early fetal malformations

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnosis of acute Zika virus infection during pregnancy with severe congenital anomalies

evidence_items.source_quote: Her blood tested negative in Trinidad by real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for dengue and chikungunya viruses, but was positive for ZIKV.

rationale: A 29-year-old pregnant woman infected with Zika virus at 9-weeks gestation in Trinidad who presented with fever, rash, and myalgias. RT-PCR was repeatedly positive for ZIKV RNA in maternal blood and subsequently in fetal tissues (placenta, umbilical cord, and fetal brain) with Sanger sequencing confirmation (E1 confirmatory evidence). Single patient dyad, current episode, primary diagnosis confirmed. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 28-year-old pregnant female with confirmed vertical Zika transmission and severe fetal brain anomalies

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnosis of vertical Zika virus transmission confirmed by amniotic fluid RT-PCR

evidence_items.source_quote: She went to the hospital, where ZIKV was presumed, and RT-PCR of the amniotic fluid was done, with a positive result at 12 weeks of gestation. The findings confirmed ZIKV vertical transmission and congenital infection.

rationale: A 28-year-old pregnant female presenting with severe fetal brain malformations. RT-PCR performed on amniotic fluid at 12 weeks gestation was positive for ZIKV, confirming vertical transmission and congenital Zika infection (E1 confirmatory evidence). Single patient dyad, current gestational episode, primary diagnosis confirmed. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 25-year-old pregnant female with acute Zika infection and congenital Zika syndrome in fetus

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnosis of acute Zika virus infection during pregnancy confirmed by RT-PCR

evidence_items.source_quote: A ZIKV infection was suspected and RT-PCR was performed, which showed a positive result at 10 weeks of gestation.

rationale: A 25-year-old pregnant woman presenting with acute rash, conjunctival hyperemia, fever, and arthralgia at 10 weeks of gestation. RT-PCR confirmed positive for ZIKV RNA (E1 confirmatory evidence), resulting in subsequent fetal microcephaly and intracranial calcifications. Single patient dyad, current episode, primary diagnosis confirmed. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 24-year-old pregnant female with vertical Zika virus infection and fetal ventriculomegaly

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnosis of vertical Zika virus infection confirmed by amniotic fluid quantitative RT-PCR

evidence_items.source_quote: This finding was confirmed with a specific ZIKV quantitative RT-PCR assay. The National Health Institute in Colombia (NHI) reported serological and virologic evidence of infection at 36 weeks of gestation, with RT-PCR positivity in the amniotic liquid for ZIKV.

rationale: A 24-year-old pregnant female from Colombia with acute rash illness during pregnancy whose fetus developed ventriculomegaly. Specific quantitative RT-PCR testing of amniotic fluid confirmed the presence of ZIKV RNA at 31 and 36 weeks gestation (E1 confirmatory evidence). Single patient dyad, current episode, primary diagnosis confirmed. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 33-year-old male presenting with Guillain-Barré syndrome caused by Zika virus

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnosis of Guillain-Barré syndrome triggered by Zika virus infection

evidence_items.source_quote: On the second day of admission, serology was positive for Zika virus (IgG antibodies).

rationale: A 33-year-old male presenting with acute fever, ascending paresthesias, flaccid quadriplegia, and respiratory failure diagnosed with Guillain-Barré syndrome caused by Zika virus. On the second day of admission, serology was positive for Zika virus (IgG antibodies) (E2 evidence supporting clinical diagnosis in post-infectious neuroinvasive disease). Single patient, current episode, primary diagnosis confirmed. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 28-year-old pregnant female with Guillain-Barré syndrome, spontaneous abortion, and confirmed Zika infection in placental/fetal tissues

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnosis of Zika virus infection confirmed by specific staining in placental and fetal tissues

evidence_items.source_quote: (in further sections of this paper, diagnosis of ZIKV infection was confirmed by specific staining in placental and fetal tissues).
evidence_items.test_name: Specific staining (IHC/ISH) for ZIKV in placental and fetal tissues

rationale: A 28-year-old pregnant woman presenting with acute rash followed by Guillain-Barré syndrome and spontaneous abortion. Although peripheral blood IgM serology was non-reactive weeks post-symptom onset, diagnosis of ZIKV infection was definitively confirmed by specific staining (IHC and ISH) in placental and fetal tissues (E1 confirmatory evidence). Single patient, current episode, primary diagnosis confirmed. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Case 2: 23-year-old pregnant woman with acute Zika virus infection

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnosis of acute Zika virus infection during pregnancy confirmed by qPCR and PRNT

evidence_items.source_quote: the qPCR was positive for Zika in serum (820 copies/ml) and urine (160 copies/ml).

rationale: A 23-year-old pregnant female presenting with fever, arthralgia, exanthema, and pruritus in the third trimester. qPCR was positive for Zika virus in serum (820 copies/mL) and urine (160 copies/mL), accompanied by positive IgM and PRNT90% (E1 confirmatory evidence). Single patient, current episode, primary diagnosis confirmed. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Case 3: 21-year-old pregnant woman with confirmed Zika virus infection

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnosis of Zika virus infection in pregnancy confirmed by IgM and PRNT90%

evidence_items.source_quote: Her IgM serology for ZIKV was positive and non-reactive for dengue, chikungunya, rubella, toxoplasmosis, HIV, syphilis and cytomegalovirus. The PRNT90% was positive for neutralizing antibodies.

rationale: A 21-year-old pregnant female presenting with fever in the second trimester. IgM serology was positive for ZIKV (and non-reactive for dengue, chikungunya, and other agents) and confirmed by positive PRNT90% neutralizing antibodies (E2 strong algorithmic evidence). Single patient, current episode, primary diagnosis confirmed. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 50-year-old female presenting with acute Zika virus infection

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnosis of acute Zika virus infection confirmed by urine RT-qPCR and viral isolation

rationale: A 50-year-old female presenting with acute fever, headache, rash, arthralgia, and prostration. Single patient, current episode, primary diagnosis confirmed. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.
